title: Global access safelist and residency request routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Establish a repeatable intake and automated routing policy for customer requests that include safelisting specific IP ranges, regional data residency constraints, and explicit failover region requirements. The goal is to reduce manual adjudication time, standardize entitlements offered to enterprise customers, and ensure requests are routed to the correct cross-functional queue (Networking, Infra, Legal, Sales Engineering) with a clear SLA and scoring outcome.
intake_form_fields: IP safelist ranges (CIDR) and expected egress locations
Estimated QPS and average request size
Has the customer completed an enterprise onboarding checklist? (link)
scoring_rubric: 1. Business criticality (0-5): revenue at risk, contract clause, strategic account
2. Data sovereignty severity (0-5): storage residency vs processing residency vs backup-only
3. Operational complexity (0-5): new region provisioning, hardware needs, support hours
4. Security/compliance burden (0-5): requires HSM/KMS, dedicated network, audits
5. Run cost delta (0-5): estimated incremental monthly cost to Redwood

Decision thresholds: 14+ => Auto-approve for dedicated engagement and SE handoff; 8-13 => Requires legal/compliance review and ENG feasibility; <=7 => Triage for self-serve or deny with suggested alternatives
triage_matrix: Combine customer score and existing regional capacity: (A) Score>=14 & capacity available -> Route to SalesEng + Infra for committed capacity proposal; (B) Score 8-13 or Score>=14 & capacity constrained -> Route to Cross-functional Review (Legal/Compliance/Infra) with canary/fallback plan; (C) Score<=7 -> Return templated alternatives (edge-routing + encryption) and recommend Dedicated evaluation if requirements increase.
routing_rules: Requests marked 'Private' or with 'regulated' classification must be routed to Legal and Security automatically. Any request that includes IP safelisting with > /24 ranges must trigger Networking and Infra review. If requested timeline is < 30 days and the score >=10, flag as 'expedite' and set 10-business-day SLA for initial response. For failover-only requests, check whether existing geo-failover maps cover the requested destinations; if yes, offer configuration change as first-line solution. Otherwise proceed to full adjudication.
acceptance_criteria: A templated intake form implemented in the Support & Sales portal
Automation rule in Linear that assigns queue based on score and classification
Standard SLA tags applied to issues (expedite / normal / deferred)
Playbook pages for SalesEng, Networking, Legal describing expected artifacts and decision checkpoints
Two pilot adjudications completed and closed with stakeholder sign-off
required_artifacts: Contract clause or customer letter of instruction (PDF/URL)
Topology diagram showing requested failover/egress points
timeline_slas: Initial triage: 3 business days; Security/legal feedback: 10 business days; Infra feasibility + cost estimate: 10 business days after triage; Final commercial proposal: 15 business days after feasibility sign-off. Expedited requests aim for 10 business day total turnaround.
rollout_constraints: Any approved new region or residency exception must include a rollback plan, fallbacks to closest region, and a capacity reservation commit for at least the first 90 days. Changes to routing require a scheduled maintenance window unless covered by emergency override by infra on-call.
